formal.strategy: Testing discipline ensures reliable software by systematically verifying correctness. First, write multiple test cases, not just one, to avoid overconfidence from a single success. Check boundary cases (like minimum/maximum values) where bugs are most likely. Include negative tests to confirm the system handles invalid input safely. Finally, use property checks to validate general behaviors across many inputs, ensuring consistency beyond specific examples.

Debugging involves reproducing the issue, tracing the program's execution to identify the first point where the state differs from a known-good run, isolating and fixing the cause at that point, and then rerunning the entire process to verify the fix.

Read each line of code in order. Before each line, note the current value of every variable. After each line, update the variables based on the operation. Keep a running list of changes to track how values evolve step by step.
